title: If you do Every Brilliant Thing and Burnout Paradise in the same day ...
transcript: I got to revisit two of my favourite fringe shows now in their New York versions, both on Broadway and off and y'all, I still love both of them so much. Every brilliant thing and Burnout Paradise are currently playing in New York. Burnout Paradise is this delightfully insane piece of theatre slash performance art that features four performers and then their host running on treadmills trying to complete a series of tasks that really explores burnout culture, but also, I feel, explores community. I have seen the show twice now. One of my favourite things about it is that it is not in your self interest to help these people out, right? And yet you feel compelled to. It makes it enjoyable and you feel the sense of human connection and wanting to provide assistance and it's just. It's just so much fun. There's a ton of audience participation in Burnout Paradise, so get ready to jump from your seats, though, if you do not want to participate at all, you do not have to. And there's. There's even small participation that you can do from your seat, like help take a photo and send it to their email, or just even asking for a cup of Gatorade. And yes, they do give you free Gatorade in the show if you want it. I did get an invite to go see Burnout Paradise, but they do offer discount tickets. There's a digital rush on today. Takes tickets are as low as $40 full price. And they do incorporate to the balcony. You wouldn't be able to run up on stage, but there definitely is audience participation in the balcony as well. I will also say there were a lot of kids at the performance that I went to, and this is a great show to bring your entire family. It's a ton of fun. Every single kid that was there was having an absolute blast. They were participating to their hearts content. There's a couple tasks that they do ask for adults, but, uh, it really great family show, honestly. And then, of course, Every Brilliant Thing, which is currently playing on Broadway, starring Daniel Radcliffe, followed by Mariska Hargitay, who's coming in to the show. Technically four, because this is the same production that was in the West End, but, uh, different staging, different performer. It just hits all the right emotional notes for me. Every Brilliant Thing tells the story of a narrator who is compiling a list of every brilliant thing that they can think of that they start after their mother's first attempt at taking her own life. So it does deal with very Very dark themes, and yet this play is so freaking joyous. And I, I've said it before, two people, but I do think, you know, there are definitely trigger warnings with this play. But. But I have seen people with depression like myself be unsure on whether they should go see this or not. And I will tell you full chest that this play has saved my life on multiple accounts. Tickets to this are insanely expensive. I was able to get a ticket from my friend who ended up having an extra ticket. There is an in person rush for this. I will let you know, however, that people are getting in line as early as 3:00am. So if you, if you have the patience. I do think this is a beautiful play and it should be seen by people. I will also say that I have seen incredible regional productions of this show as well. So if it's out of your price range, if you can see this anywhere near you, I highly recommend it. But Daniel Radcliffe is in fact incredible and you should try to see it on Broadway if you can. If You have it within your means and can't afford to do so. I do really, really, really adore this play, and I definitely think for both of these, there is something that you lose from not having the intimacy of the fringe environment. So if you've got to see them at a friend, I will say mileage may vary, I do think that both of them are still absolutely fantastic pieces of theatre, even in these slightly too significantly larger spaces. And both of these shows are under 90 minutes, so they're great if you're trying to get to a concert afterwards or just trying to get home. If you're looking for a shorter show to squeeze into your day, Every Brilliant Thing does do five PM show times, so always a great option.
